observation_summary: The Closure Compiler was aggressively removing unused function parameters even in SIMPLE_OPTIMIZATIONS mode, which broke code relying on the Function.length property (e.g., for currying).
hypothesis: The optimization pass that removes unused function arguments was being applied unconditionally, failing to respect the constraints of the compilation mode (SIMPLE_OPTIMIZATIONS).
prediction: The code would show a missing conditional check that prevents the removal of unused function arguments when global optimization is not enabled.
experiment_rationale: The fix adds a guard clause `if (!removeGlobals) { return; }` at the beginning of the function responsible for removing unused arguments, confirming that the logic was missing a necessary check for the compilation context.
reasoning_summary: The fix is a classic 'Checking' defect: a missing guard condition (`if (!removeGlobals)`) was added to prevent an optimization pass from executing in a context where it was inappropriate (SIMPLE_OPTIMIZATIONS). This is not an algorithmic error (the removal logic itself is correct) nor a design capability gap (the feature exists, it was just applied too broadly).
evidence_used: The fix adds a conditional check: if (!removeGlobals) { return; }
The bug report states that SIMPLE_OPTIMIZATIONS should not remove function parameters because it breaks the length property.
The fix diff shows the addition of a guard clause in RemoveUnusedVars.java.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: The removal logic itself is not incorrect; the issue is that it is being applied in the wrong context. The fix is a guard, not a change to the removal algorithm.
This is not a missing design capability; it is an over-eager application of an existing optimization pass.
